speaker: Unknown
text: Key thirteen, with a blank tag. Unlucky for somebody.

speaker: Unknown
text: The key to the great doors. Heavy, the way important things are.

speaker: Unknown
text: I have the one I need. The rest can stay mysterious.

speaker: Unknown
text: Forty iron keys and not a single label.

speaker: Unknown
text: Number thirteen, the book said. Of course it did.

speaker: Unknown
text: I could try them all. Or I could find out which one I want.

speaker: Unknown
text: Dead lanterns. A whole shelf of light, all of it out.

speaker: Unknown
text: The way back out to the gate.

speaker: Unknown
text: A gatekeeper's lodge. The door is open. Graveyards are trusting places.

speaker: Unknown
text: The choir loft. You can feel how loud it used to be.

speaker: Unknown
text: The stair, back down to the cloister.

speaker: Unknown
text: Nothing else in there I'd want to explain owning.

speaker: Unknown
text: A crow's nest. Twigs, wire, and everything that ever glittered in this cemetery.

speaker: Unknown
text: A lantern glass, nested in pride of place. Sorry, crow.

speaker: Unknown
text: The stone's still rough where the chisel went. As if it happened yesterday.

speaker: Unknown
text: Chisel marks, careful ones. Whoever did this took pride in it.

speaker: Unknown
text: Smooth stone, a few scratches deep. The name was here.

speaker: Unknown
text: Organ pipes, bent like old men.

speaker: Unknown
text: Silent. Of course it is.

speaker: Unknown
text: Bones, stacked like firewood. Somebody here had a very tidy mind.

speaker: Unknown
text: Back up to the gate.

speaker: Unknown
text: A lantern on a pole. Iron frame, no glass. A lantern in principle only.

speaker: Unknown
text: "U..." Then a smudge. "Paid by a dove."

speaker: Unknown
text: "Stone defaced by order of the Registrar." A whole order, just for my stone.

speaker: Unknown
text: And in the margin: "Ossuary: key thirteen."

speaker: Unknown
text: Burials, one a line, for years. Hardly any names left in it. Just dates and plots.

speaker: Unknown
text: Dead roses, still holding on to the columns. Stubborn.

speaker: Unknown
text: Gold, and candles, and one voice above all the others.

speaker: Unknown
text: She was singing names. A list of them, like a prayer.

speaker: Unknown
text: I was there. I know I was. So why can't I see myself?

speaker: Unknown
text: Goodbye.

speaker: Unknown
text: I need to get into the city.

speaker: Unknown
text: Did you know someone called the dove?

speaker: Unknown
text: Who are you?

speaker: Sister
text: That's her hand. In the margins.

speaker: Sister
text: Names. She wrote them down, so that somebody would remember them.

speaker: Sister
text: Take the key. Whoever you were, she'd have wanted you to go and find out.

speaker: Sister
text: Go in peace. Or at least go.

speaker: Sister
text: The great doors are locked, and I have the key.

speaker: Sister
text: I don't hand it to shadows who can't tell me their own names.

speaker: Sister
text: Bring me something of hers. Her hymn book was in the loft, if the crows have left it.

speaker: Sister
text: ...We had a singer we called that. The best of us.

speaker: Sister
text: She sang a list once, in this church, that she should not have sung.

speaker: Sister
text: After that I can't remember her face. Or her name. Only the voice.

speaker: Unknown
text: A nun, standing as straight as the columns. Straighter.

speaker: Sister
text: You walk like a man who has been told he is late.

speaker: Unknown
text: I've been told I'm dead. That's later.

speaker: Sister
text: Hm. Then you'll want to be quick.

speaker: Sister
text: That isn't hers.

speaker: Sister
text: The last of the choir. We sang here every evening. Then one evening we couldn't.

speaker: Sister
text: Not a note, any of us. We still remember the words. That's the cruel part.

speaker: Sister
text: Yes?

speaker: Unknown
text: They've all got the same expression. I'd find it comforting if I had one.

speaker: Unknown
text: An empty stand. The book's with me.

speaker: Unknown
text: One stand still standing, and one book still open on it.

speaker: Unknown
text: A stove, cold as everything else.

speaker: Unknown
text: A sundial in the moonlight. It doesn't tell the time. Nothing here does.

speaker: Unknown
text: Pitch dark up there, and the steps are worn to nothing. I'd want a light.

speaker: Unknown
text: The lantern makes a small, brave circle. It'll do.

speaker: Unknown
text: A stair turret, up to the choir loft.

speaker: Unknown
text: A well, dry to the bottom. I'd make a wish, but I can't think what I'd want.

speaker: Unknown
text: A saint, still waiting for someone to pray to her.

speaker: Unknown
text: I don't think it's going to be me.
